extracted.intended_audience: Scientists invited to review manuscripts for EMBO Press journals (EMBO Journal, EMBO Reports, EMBO Molecular Medicine, Molecular Systems Biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers assessing life-science manuscripts submitted to EMBO Press journals, describing reviewer responsibilities, conflicts of interest, report structure, and editorial expectations for content and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript triage for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted manuscripts are assessed by the editors for suitability for the review process. To save authors and reviewers time, only those manuscripts judged most likely to meet our editorial criteria are sent out for formal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may send manuscripts to Advisory Editorial Board members for further input before deciding whether to send out for formal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that are sent for peer review typically go to three reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on reviewers' advice the editor decides to accept, invite revision, or reject; reviewers' reports feed into an editorial judgement rather than a simple vote count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are not a matter of counting votes or numerical rank assessments, but rather are based on an evaluation of the strengths of the arguments raised by each reviewer and by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most useful reviewer reports are those that set out clear, substantiated arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent review process / publication of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press makes the editorial process transparent for all accepted manuscripts by publishing the reviewer reports alongside published papers, as well as all correspondence between authors and the editors relevant to the decision process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer anonymity will be strictly maintained. Reviewers should note their reports and the authors' point-by-point responses will be included in this document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Factually incorrect statements should be avoided, and arguments in favour or disfavour of a given study should be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to be very clear about what revision will be required for a manuscript to become acceptable so that it is apparent how to proceed without additional consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journals do not ask for 'confidential comments to the editor'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urgent further issues that cannot be included in the reviewer report, in particular concerns about ethical standards, data integrity, biosecurity or conflicts of an academic or commercial nature, should be communicated directly to the editor via email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-to-reviewer commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: To enhance the consistency of the peer-review process, the editors provide the opportunity for reviewers to comment on each other's reports before making their decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows extreme opinions to be scrutinised at an early point and mistakes to be detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting reviews with preprints (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have the option to request that the journal posts reviews obtained via peer review at the journal alongside a preprint version of the manuscript on bio/medRxiv, including an author response to the reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above, reviewer anonymity is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection is based on a balance of factors, including expertise, scientific reputation, and our previous experience with the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts are sent to reviewers only after having contacted them about the possibility first, and reviewers should treat this initial request as confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and prompt communication
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO Press is committed to rapid editorial decisions and publication; reviewers should respond promptly or inform the editors if they anticipate a significant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check the deadline on receipt and contact the editorial office immediately if you anticipate any difficulties in meeting it; notifying delays allows editors to keep authors informed and find alternative reviewers if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial actions on receiving a manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a manuscript, reviewers should double-check the deadline, consider whether there might be a conflict of interest, and whether they can judge the article impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the editorial office immediately if you anticipate difficulty meeting the deadline or if you identify potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should treat the review process with strict confidence. Manuscripts should not be discussed with anyone not directly involved in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If colleagues are consulted, they should be identified to the editors. If experts from outside the reviewer’s own laboratory are consulted, reviewers should check with the editors beforehand to avoid involving anyone who may have been excluded by the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and identity disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not disclose their identities to the authors or to other colleagues since they may be asked to comment on the criticisms of other reviewers and may then find it difficult to be objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should reviewers feel strongly about making their identities known to the authors, they should do so via the editor and also have the option to sign their report. Reviewers are discouraged from confirming or denying speculation about their identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-review implies that the co-reviewer is supervised to provide an authoritative, professional reviewer report and the primary reviewer explicitly agrees with all the points raised by the co-reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-review with other senior colleagues may be possible but requires pre-consultation with the editor as the co-reviewer might have been excluded by the authors. Co-reviewers must be named in the dedicated text box in the reviewer form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of reviewer reports is to provide the editors with the information that they need to reach a decision, but they should also instruct the authors on how to strengthen their manuscript if revision is a possibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should enable editors to decide and give clear actionable guidance to authors about required revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and conduct in reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to maintain a critical but constructive and impartial attitude in evaluating manuscripts. Criticisms should remain dispassionate; offensive language is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A negative report should explain to the authors the weaknesses of their manuscript so they can understand the basis for a decision. EMBO may edit reports to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information; reviewers should avoid causing needless offence but understand that robust language may not be unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured report components
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports tend to follow the following general structure: Summary; General remarks; Major points; Minor points; Presentation and style; Trivial mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary should describe understanding of the story, key conclusions, and methodology/model system. General remarks should state whether you are convinced of key conclusions, place the work in context, state nature and significance of advance, and identify the audience. Major points should list specific criticisms related to key conclusions, specify experiments/analyses required, and motivate critiques with relevant citations and argumentation. Minor points are easily addressable points; Presentation and style includes trivial mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major points content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Major points should contain specific criticisms related to key conclusions and specify experiments or analyses required to demonstrate the conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivate critiques with relevant citations and argumentation so editors and authors understand the basis for required work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest identification and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing reviewer/advisor interests exist if the reviewer/advisor is currently engaged in, is planning to engage in or would consider engaging in, related experiments that could benefit from unpublished information acquired from the manuscript under consideration, has financial or commercial interests or previous personal or professional connection to the authors. This information must be shared with the editor regardless of the reviewers’ level of support for the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to decide whether they have competing interests based on the abstract and author list (for non-blinded papers) before they accept to review the manuscript. Decline if unable to be objective. If a reviewer accepts and later discovers a competing interest, notify the editor immediately and permanently delete any accessed manuscript files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples requiring consultation with the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples where reviewers should consult with the editor include: the author and reviewer previously worked closely together; employed by the same institute (with nuance regarding institute size and interaction); the reviewer sits on a scientific advisory board that approved the authors’ research proposal; editorial conflicts (reviewer is an editor at a competing journal); former advisors/mentees within the past 10 years (recommended to avoid); or when a reviewer disagrees a priori with the conclusions or the research presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each case will be decided individually; reviewers should alert editors to anything that might affect neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alerting editors to ethical or publication policy concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: In spite of best efforts to identify breaches of publication policy or ethical conduct, reviewers who are more familiar with the field are more likely to recognise such problems and should alert the editors to any potential problems in this regard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns include plagiarism, author conflict of interest, data integrity, and other ethical issues; use direct communication to the editor for urgent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer feedback, re-review, and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: When asked to re-review a revised manuscript, reviewers will normally be sent copies of the other reviewers' comments. Upon request, the editors inform reviewers of decisions and send copies of the other reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers who find their recommendations overruled should recognise that experts can disagree. EMBO collaborates with ORCID and Web of Science to allow reviewers to record and receive recognition for peer review contributions.
